items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep scheduling running requests after a priority self-preemption
items.body:
## Purpose

Under `--scheduling-policy priority`, when a running request cannot get KV blocks the scheduler preempts the lowest-priority running request. `self.running` is in admission order, not priority order, so that request can sit in the middle of the list, for example when higher-priority requests arrived after it. If it is the request currently being scheduled, it preempts itself, and the running loop then `break`s:

```python
if new_blocks is None:
    # Cannot schedule this request.
    break
```

Every running request after it gets no tokens in that step, even though they all have higher priority, the self-preemption just freed blocks, and budget remains. This is a priority inversion: the requests the policy is meant to protect lose a step whenever a lower-priority request ahead of them runs out of KV.

After a self-preemption the request has already been removed from `self.running` (`del self.running[victim_index]` with `victim_index == req_index`), so `req_index` already points at the next request. The fix continues the loop in that case. Nothing changes for FCFS: it preempts `running[-1]`, so a self-preemption there only happens on the last request. Other reasons for a failed allocation (a deferred free that will not help, pending connector frees) still end the loop.

Related but different: #49097 (fixed by #49206) adjusted `req_index` when the victim sits before the cursor. #39375, a larger rework of this preemption path that has been open since March, would also remove this `break`.

## Test Plan

- New `test_priority_self_preemption_keeps_scheduling_later_running_requests`. Setup: one free block, `running = [A(p0), B(p5), C(p0)]`; A and B both need a new block on the same decode step, C does not. A takes the block, B preempts itself, and C must still be scheduled.
- `tests/v1/core` in full, main vs this PR.
- A random-workload stall check on the real `Scheduler` (small per-step budgets, priority/FCFS mixed, hybrid attention+Mamba and full-attention layouts, 40 seeds each). It flags a running request that gets 0 tokens while the step has budget left for its whole remainder; this is how I found it.

## Test Result

(CPU only.)

- New test: fails on main (`{'A': 1}` scheduled, C skipped), passes with this PR.

- Stall check, hybrid layout: main stalls on 1/40 seeds (this bug), this PR on 0/40. Full-attention layout: 0/40 on both, with identical per-run action counts. A KV-content check over 60 more seeds on this PR found nothing.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep Mamba-aligned prefill chunks out of the MTP lookahead window
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #61762.

With Mamba `align` prefix caching (the default for hybrid models once prefix caching is on) and multi-module MTP (`num_prefill_lookahead = num_speculative_tokens = L >= 2`), a prompt that ends 1..L-1 tokens past a Mamba block boundary can stop being scheduled. Two clamps in `Scheduler.schedule()` disagree about the same position:

1. `_mamba_block_aligned_split` ends a chunk on a block boundary (a cacheable checkpoint, or a budget-limited chunk floored to a boundary).
2. `_reserve_prefill_lookahead` sees fewer than L tokens left and moves the end back by `L - remaining`, off the boundary.
3. On the next step the chunk starts mid-block, the split stops it at that same boundary, the reservation shortens it to 0, and the request is skipped. This repeats on every step: the request holds its KV blocks and never finishes, and no error is raised.

The report in #61762 (and my follow-up there) only showed this with `disable_eagle_block_drop=True`. While writing the fix I found it also happens with EAGLE block drop on (the default) whenever the chunk that reaches the last boundary is budget-limited. Block size 16, L=3, 49-token prompt, 16-token budget: the chunks end at 16, 32, then 46, and from then on 0 tokens per step. With a shared per-step budget, a long prompt's last full chunk can be budget-limited in this way.

**Fix.** The lookahead is now resolved inside `_mamba_block_aligned_split`, which knows where chunks may end. If a chunk would end inside the window, the split does the first of these that applies:

- **Finish the prefill**, if the budget allows it and it crosses no block boundary from a mid-block start. This gives up the checkpoint inside the window.
- **Stop at the last block boundary before the window.**
- **Keep the aligned end.** `_reserve_prefill_lookahead` now leaves Mamba-aligned ends alone, so the next chunk finishes the prefill. In that case the drafter reads sampled tokens at this one boundary, which is what the reservation tries to avoid. That is a draft-quality cost; the alternatives are a livelock, or a chunk ending mid-block followed by one crossing the boundary, which publishes a Mamba slot at the wrong offset (#43559).

Unaligned (sub-block) chunk ends are still shortened by `_reserve_prefill_lookahead` as before. Nothing changes when `num_prefill_lookahead <= 1` (EAGLE-family drafters, or no drafter). The window condition `N - L < end < N` cannot hold in that case.

## Reachability

As far as I can tell, no public checkpoint reaches this today:
- Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next have one MTP layer.
- Ling/Ring-2.5 and Kimi-Linear have none.
- `nemotron_h_mtp.py` asserts a single MTP layer.

`qwen3_next_mtp.py` and `bailing_moe_v3_mtp.py` already iterate over `num_nextn_predict_layers`, and nothing rejects multi-module MTP with `align`. A hybrid checkpoint with two or more MTP layers would hit it. All evidence below is scheduler-level on CPU. I have not run a model, and I am not claiming end-to-end validation.

## Test Plan

- `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py::test_mamba_split_respects_multi_module_mtp_prefill_lookahead` (216 cases).
  - Each step runs the real `_mamba_block_aligned_split` and then `_reserve_prefill_lookahead`, allocating through a real hybrid `KVCacheManager`.
  - Parameters: Mamba block 64/1600, L 2/3/5, prompt tail inside/at the edge of/past the window, 1–2 full blocks, budget 4 blocks / 1 block / half a block (the sub-block mode), EAGLE block drop on/off.
  - It asserts that the prefill completes, that non-final chunk ends are block-aligned when the budget allows it, and that a chunk ends inside the window only on a boundary and only when it cannot finish. It also runs the file's existing `_count_cached_boundary_states` check, which verifies that every hash-cached Mamba slot holds the state its hash claims.
- `test_mamba_split_lookahead_window_is_noop_without_multi_module_mtp`: L=0/1 keep today's split.
- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_mamba_align_multi_module_mtp_prefill_does_not_livelock`: the real `Scheduler`, with the cases from #61762.
- Stubs passed as `self` to `_mamba_block_aligned_split` in four test files gain `num_prefill_lookahead=0`, so those tests are unchanged.

## Test Result

(CPU only, WSL Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12; my local environment lacks `torchvision`, which affects a few unrelated tests on both trees.)

- New tests on main's code (this PR's tests applied to `71536bd5f8`): **124 failed, 143 passed**. Of the failures, 72 are block-drop-off cases, 48 are block-drop-on (default) cases, all with a budget of one block or less, and 4 are the `Scheduler` cases. With this PR: **267 passed**.
- `tests/v1/core` in full, main vs this PR: the failed/errored sets are identical (68 environment failures on both trees: missing `torchvision` and offline model configs), with 0 failures only on this PR; passes go from 940 to 1161 (the new tests).
- Repro from #61762 (block 16, budget 512): main stalls at 46/49; this PR finishes, scheduling 0→49 in one chunk.
- Default EAGLE block drop, budget 16 (49/50-token prompts, L=3; 33-token prompt, L=2): main stalls at 46/47/31; this PR finishes. Budgets ≥ 32 show identical chunking before and after.
- I also ran a random-workload stall check: the real `Scheduler` on a hybrid attention+Mamba config, 40 seeds × 300 steps per config. It flags a running request that gets 0 tokens while the step has budget left for its whole remainder.
  - L=3 with block drop off: main has 16/40 seeds stalled, this PR has 0.
  - L=2 with block drop off: main has 14/40, this PR has 1. The one remaining seed is a harness artifact: a preempted 304-token request plus spec lookahead slots needs more blocks than the 24-block pool has, and its split/reservation results are the same as on main.
  - L=3 with block drop on, and L=1: 0 stalls on both trees, with identical per-run action counts, so scheduling is unchanged there.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass (ruff check/format, typos, mypy, SPDX, new-test CI wiring).

items.title: [Fix] Warn when unsupported Anthropic system content is ignored
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61172. The Anthropic entrypoint's system conversion silently drops any non-`text` content block (e.g. an `image` block) both in the top-level `system` field (`_convert_system_message`) and in inline system messages (`_extract_system_text`). The OpenAI endpoint already warns about this (#34072) but the Anthropic path never did, so unsupported blocks vanished without a trace.

## Claims

- Emit a `logger.warning_once` naming the dropped content type when an unsupported Anthropic system content block is ignored, mirroring the OpenAI endpoint's wording.
- `tool_addition` / `tool_removal` blocks in inline system messages do not warn: they are not ignored, `_resolve_tools` applies them to the tool list (review feedback).
- Keep the existing behavior of ignoring unsupported blocks (backward compatible) — only the warning is added.

## Validation

- `ruff check` / `ruff format` (0.14.0) and mypy clean.
- `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py` + `test_protocol_exports.py`: 116 passed on the branch and on a merge with main `87e7dce3a7`.
- New regression tests: top-level and inline image blocks warn while text is preserved; text-only / string / billing-header cases do not warn; tool changes do not warn and are still applied; a mixed message warns only for the image block (inline and merged-system paths).
- The tool-change tests fail on the previous head and pass now. The warning tests use the existing `disable_log_dedup` fixture; without it, the inline-image test depended on test order.

## Details

Root cause: `_convert_system_message` / `_extract_system_text` drop any content block whose type is not `text` without notifying the caller, so callers can pass e.g. `system: [{"type":"image",...}]` and have it silently ignored. The fix keeps the drop (backward compatibility) but surfaces it with a once-per-type warning.

## Overview

`LLM.score()` wrote the model's pooling task into the `PoolingParams` object the caller passed in, so reusing a `PoolingParams()` with another pooling model failed before any inference ran. #58842 fixed the same footgun for the other offline pooling entry points; this applies the same one-line pattern to the scoring path, which it left untouched.

## Claims

- `LLM.score()` no longer modifies the caller's `PoolingParams`: the task is filled in on a clone, matching `LLM.encode()` / `embed()` / `classify()`.
- An explicitly conflicting `task` still raises the same `ValueError`; nothing else changes.

## Validation

The original regression failed on unpatched main (1 failed, 1 passed), then passed with the parameter clone. Following review, the caller-ownership regression and its helper now live in `tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_io_processor.py`; the separate file and redundant conflicting-task case were removed

Current focused run on commit `ec22afe9b829e95159d2a66d9e24addcb6fa50c6`:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu /home/dcl/projects/vllm-v2-gpu-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_io_processor.py tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_factories.py tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_utils.py -q --tb=short
```

## Details

Root cause: unlike the other offline pooling entry points, `score()` filled in the task inline on the object it was handed:

```python

if pooling_params.task is None:

```

`encode()` / `embed()` / `classify()` only forward the parameters and clone them downstream (#58842: `base/io_processor.py`, `pooling/io_processor.py`). Every `pooling_params.task` write in `offline.py` was checked: the scoring path was the only remaining one, so the same one-line clone is applied there instead of restructuring anything.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Keep store pins and AbortAck until NIXL transfers stop

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

items.body:
## Overview

The P2P producer released store pins, and sent `AbortAck` to the consumer, while its NIXL WRITEs could still be running. Neither cancelling the handle nor removing the remote peer stops a running WRITE with the UCX backend. This PR keeps the pins, and holds back `AbortAck`, until NIXL reports each transfer terminal. Addresses #59569 and the review on this PR. The consumer-side counterpart is tracked in #61532.

## Claims

- `NixlTransport.cancel(mode="wait")` releases only transfers that are no longer `PROC`/`PEND`. Previously it reported running WRITEs as cancelled, because `release_xfer_handle` never fails for an in-progress UCX request.
- A round whose store timed out, or which the consumer aborted, fails its jobs but keeps the pins of jobs that inflight transfers still read, until those transfers are terminal. Late completions settle each job exactly once, and new supply cannot restart such a round.
- The abort drain no longer falls back to `cancel(mode="immediate")` + `AbortAck` after `_CANCEL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S`. Past the timeout it logs once and keeps retrying. `AbortAck` is sent only when no transfer of the round can still write to the consumer.
- Wait-mode cancel retries are paced to one attempt per round per 100 ms, shared by the store-timeout sweep and the abort drain.
- When one transfer of a round fails, the round's other transfers are no longer cancelled with `mode="immediate"`. The round is marked cancelled instead: their pins and the round's `TransferDoneMsg(success=False)` wait until they are terminal.
- `nixlRemoteDisconnectError` from `check_xfer_state`, which NIXL raises when the peer process is gone, is treated as a terminal failure, so a dead peer no longer pins its transfers until the session closes.

## Validation

Real NIXL 1.4.1, UCX over TCP, CPU DRAM. This is not RDMA hardware.

| scenario | result |
|---|---|
| 512 MiB WRITE, old `cancel(mode="wait")` | returned `[]` while `PROC` in 5/5 runs; all bytes landed afterwards |
| 512 MiB WRITE, new `cancel(mode="wait")` | returned the tid as still inflight in 5/5 runs; `poll()` reported DONE only after all 512 MiB landed |
| 512 MiB WRITE, `remove_remote_peer` | returned with 14–392 MB landed in 5/5 runs; the rest still landed, and the handle then raises `nixlNotFoundError` |
| 1 GiB WRITE stalled by SIGSTOPping the target, then `cancel(mode="immediate")` + `remove_remote_peer`, then resume | 64/64 blocks still landed |
| stalled WRITE, target left stopped | stays `PROC` for 60 s, no timeout of its own |
| stalled WRITE, target SIGKILLed | `check_xfer_state` raises `nixlRemoteDisconnectError` |

Unit tests use the fake transport in `test_sessions.py` and a mocked NIXL agent in `test_data_transport.py`. The new behavior tests fail on the respective previous logic and pass now.

```sh
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ -q
# head 387b0ba092 (agent-run):  486 passed, 1 skipped
# head 84ec0d792f (I ran it myself, and the agent independently): 484 passed, 1 skipped, 14 warnings in 78.57s
```

ruff 0.14.0 and mypy 1.20.2 (`tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.12`) are clean.

Not done: RDMA/InfiniBand hardware, GPU memory, serving load or model evaluation.

## Details

**Root cause.** `NixlTransport.cancel(mode="wait")` relied on `release_xfer_handle` raising for a transfer that is still running. With UCX it never raises: `nixlUcxBackendReqH::release` calls `ucp_request_cancel`, which does nothing for an RMA PUT, then frees the request and returns success. The producer therefore treated running WRITEs as cancelled, released their store pins, and acked aborts while bytes were still landing. `remove_remote_peer` → `invalidateRemoteMD` only drops the connection entry, and the endpoint is later closed in flush mode, so outstanding writes complete rather than stop. That rules out the suggested "tear down the peer, then ack" fallback.

**Abort flow after this change.**
1. The consumer sends `AbortFetchMsg`.
2. The producer marks the round cancelled, fails the jobs no transfer reads, and keeps the rest pinned. A failed transfer takes its round down the same path.
3. It retries `cancel(mode="wait")` at the paced rate. A transfer leaves only when NIXL reports it terminal, or the peer is gone.
4. When no transfer of the round remains, the producer releases the remaining pins and sends `AbortAckMsg`. An aborted round sends no `TransferDoneMsg`.

**Tradeoff.** There is no hard deadline on the producer side. If a peer stays alive but the WRITE never progresses, the pins stay held, with one warning after `_CANCEL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S`. A bound would need a transport primitive that guarantees a running WRITE has stopped. An awaited forced endpoint close (`UCP_EP_CLOSE_FLAG_FORCE`) might be one, but NIXL does not expose it. The consumer still gives up after `_ABORT_ACK_TIMEOUT_S` and frees its slots; that is the open issue #61532.

The `store_timed_out` flag on a round is renamed `cancelled`, because it now covers aborts and failed transfers as well. All three paths share it: jobs no transfer reads fail at once, and the others keep their pins until their transfers are terminal.

The remote-disconnect check matches the binding's class name or the `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` status code, so the NIXL bindings are not imported in this module. An error it does not recognize keeps the transfer inflight, which is the conservative side.

The shutdown drain in `manager.py` still falls back to `mode="immediate"` after `_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S`, because the engine is exiting. Only its docstring is updated.

This is distinct from #59329, which withdraws timed-out parked supply before Fetch. Its withdrawal set must be derived from the results actually emitted (`{r.job_id for r in results}`), so that unconfirmed inflight jobs are not removed from the round's pending jobs. Whichever PR merges second needs that adjustment.

items.title: [Bugfix][ToolParsers] Close unterminated tool-call arguments on truncated streams
items.body:
### Summary

`HYV3ToolParser` / `HYV4ToolParser` stream tool-call arguments incrementally and intentionally **withhold the closing `}`** of the arguments JSON until `</tool_call>` arrives (so partial values can keep growing with a stable prefix). When generation ends early — `max_tokens`, `stop`, or client disconnect — the stream never sees the closing tag, and the framework's finalize step (`_append_unstreamed_tool_args`) appends `get_remaining_unstreamed_args()` to the last tool-call chunk. Both parsers returned `""` because the in-flight tool call was never registered in `prev_tool_call_arr`, so the client received an **unterminated JSON fragment** such as `{"city": "Beijing"` that cannot be parsed.

This PR:

1. Overrides `get_remaining_unstreamed_args()` in both parsers to emit the withheld JSON tail from their incremental-streaming state (`_completed_args` / `_streamed_json_len`), so a truncated stream still ends with parseable arguments (`{"city": "Beijing"}`) and complete streams are unaffected (tail is empty).

items.body:
## Summary

`suppress_stdout()` derived the fd to silence from `sys.stdout.fileno()`, which breaks in two ways (reported in #59268 and #59269):

- **#59268** — when `sys.stdout` has no fd at all (e.g. under `contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO())` or in a Jupyter kernel), `fileno()` raises `io.UnsupportedOperation`, aborting engine startup on the distributed-init path.
- **#59269** — when `sys.stdout` is bound to stderr's fd (the common `sys.stdout = sys.stderr` idiom), `dup2(devnull, 2)` silently discards stderr output, contradicting the docstring's promise to preserve error messages.

## Fix

C libraries write to `STDOUT_FILENO` regardless of what `sys.stdout` is bound to, so silence fd 1 directly and leave `sys.stdout` / `sys.stderr` alone. stderr is then never a candidate. Normal behavior (stdout suppressed while inside, restored after) is unchanged.

## Why this is not a duplicate

#59268 and #59269 are both open, have zero comments, and no linked PR. No existing PR touches `suppress_stdout`.

## Tests

New `tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py` (offline, subprocess-isolated, no GPU needed):
- fd-1 output is suppressed inside the context and restored after;
- a fd-less `sys.stdout` no longer crashes (#59268);
- stderr survives when `sys.stdout` is bound to stderr (#59269).

items.title: [Bugfix] Keep Hunyuan A13B streaming envelope open until </answer> closes
items.body:
## Summary

Fix Hunyuan A13B reasoning streaming so the closing `\n</answer>` marker no longer leaks into the streamed `content`.

## Problem

When streaming a Hunyuan A13B response, the closing `\n</answer>` marker appears verbatim in the model's `content` instead of being stripped. Non-streaming output strips it correctly via the existing regex; only streaming is affected.

Example from #58127 (decoding token ids `[14023,771,397,771,198,524,27963,397,27,9399,397,198,524,9399,29]`):

```
<think>ink</think>
<answer>answer</answer>
```

used to stream content as `answer\n</answer>`, leaking the framing marker.

## Root Cause

`HunyuanA13BReasoningParser` is a three-state token state machine: `idle -> think -> response -> idle`, where `think_start_ids`, `response_start_ids` (`\n</think>\n<answer>\n`) and `response_end_ids` (`\n</answer>`) drive transitions.

`is_reasoning_end()` returned `self.current_state == "response"`. The outer `DelegatingParser.parse_delta()` uses `is_reasoning_end_streaming()` to decide when to stop feeding deltas to the reasoning parser. As soon as the state machine consumed `<answer>` and entered the `response` state, the hand-off flipped `reasoning_ended = True`. From then on, subsequent deltas bypassed the reasoning parser and were passed straight to `content`. The state machine therefore never received the trailing `\n</answer>` tokens, which it would otherwise have buffered and suppressed.

## Solution

Override `is_reasoning_end_streaming()` so the hand-off only fires once the parser has **entered** the response region **and left it again** (i.e. the whole envelope has closed). A one-shot `_response_seen` flag is set on the `think -> response` transition.

While waiting for `</answer>`:
- the answer body is still routed to `content` by `extract_reasoning_streaming()` (non-matching tokens in the `response` state return `DeltaMessage(content=...)`);
- the closing `response_end_ids` are matched against `expected_sequence`, buffered and suppressed exactly like the start markers.

The prompt-time `is_reasoning()` contract is unchanged.

## Testing

Added `tests/reasoning/test_hunyuan_reasoning_parser.py::test_streaming_does_not_leak_closing_answer_marker`, which replays the exact token-id sequence from #58127 while mirroring `DelegatingParser.parse_delta()`'s gating (stop feeding the reasoning parser once `is_reasoning_end_streaming()` flips). It asserts `</answer>` is absent from streamed `content`. This test fails on the old code and passes with the fix.

`ruff check` clean on both changed files.

## Compatibility

Behavior change is limited to streaming output for `hunyuan_a13b`: streamed `content` no longer contains the trailing `\n</answer>`. Non-streaming extraction is untouched.

## Related

Fixes #58127

---

**Duplicate check (required before writing code).**

Two overlaps, one of them internal:

- **#58130** (cs-fisha): `[BugFix] Keep Hunyuan streaming parser stripping </answer>` —
  same file pair, and it fixes the class rather than the case, by adding an opt-in
  `post_reasoning_stream_filter` to the shared `DelegatingParser` in
  `vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py`. That is **more general than this PR**, which keeps the
  handling inside the Hunyuan state machine.
- **#58412** in this same repository is mine and touches
  `hunyuan_a13b_reasoning_parser.py` as well (multi-token streaming deltas). Two of my own
  PRs on one file is not something a reviewer should have to reconcile.

Next step, stated rather than implied: compare #58130's `post_reasoning_stream_filter`
against this patch and keep whichever single change covers both the `</answer>` stripping
and the multi-token delta cases; then close the other. Until that comparison is done this
PR stays open but should not be reviewed in isolation.

items.title: [Bugfix] Keep closing </think> delimiter in MiniMax M2 append-think mode
items.body:
## Summary

The MiniMax M2 tool parser dropped the closing `</think>` delimiter from `content`
when it appeared in the CONTENT state — i.e. when combined with the
`minimax_m2_append_think` reasoning parser, which intentionally keeps the
reasoning delimiters in `content`. The opening `<think>` survived but the
closing `</think>` was silently consumed, breaking the output contract clients
rely on to distinguish thinking from the answer / tool invocation.

## Problem

Reported in #58486. With

```
--enable-auto-tool-choice
--tool-call-parser minimax_m2
--reasoning-parser minimax_m2_append_think
```

a fixed model output like

```
I should add them.</think><minimax:tool_call><invoke name="add">...</invoke></minimax:tool_call>
```

produced `content = "<think>I should add them."` — the closing `</think>` was
missing. The tool call itself was extracted correctly; only the delimiter was
lost. This affects both streaming and non-streaming responses with
`tool_choice="auto"`.

## Root cause

`MiniMaxM2AppendThinkReasoningParser` returns `(None, "<think>" + model_output)`,
so reasoning is *not* stripped and everything — including both `</think>`
delimiters — is supposed to live in `content`. The tool parser engine then
processes this text already in the CONTENT state. In the declarative config
(`vllm/parser/minimax_m2.py`), the transition

```python
(ParserState.CONTENT, "THINK_END"): Transition(ParserState.CONTENT, ()),
```

emits no events when it matches `</think>`. That is correct for the *normal*
reasoning path (where `</think>` is the `REASONING -> CONTENT` boundary, handled
by the `REASONING/THINK_END` transition that emits `REASONING_END`), but in
append-think mode the closing delimiter is data, not a boundary — so it was
silently dropped. The `<think>` opening tag has no `CONTENT/THINK_START`
transition and therefore falls through as ordinary content, which is why only
the closing delimiter was lost.

This transition was introduced by the engine migration in #45701.

## Solution

Emit `EventType.TEXT_CHUNK` on the `(CONTENT, "THINK_END")` transition so the
matched `</think>` literal is appended to content instead of being consumed
silently. The `REASONING/THINK_END` transition still owns the normal
reasoning/end-of-reasoning boundary, so standard `minimax_m2` reasoning
extraction is unchanged.

## Testing

New regression test in `tests/parser/engine/test_minimax_m2.py`:

- `TestThinkEndInContent::test_closing_think_end_in_content_is_preserved` —
  feeds `<think>thoughts</think>answer</think>` immediately followed by a tool
  call and asserts `content == "answer</think>"` while the tool call is still
  parsed correctly.

Existing MiniMax M2 parser and reasoning-parser tests are unchanged in
expectation.

## Compatibility

- No API or config changes.
- Standard reasoning mode (`minimax_m2`, not append-think) is unaffected: the
  end-of-reasoning `</think>` still goes through `REASONING/THINK_END`. A
  literal `</think>` that genuinely appears inside answer text is now preserved
  verbatim, which is the correct literal behavior.

## Related

Fixes #58486.

## Readiness gate

Run at head `7ee4043` on a CPU-only box (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`).

**A gap in the shipped test, found by the edge-case review.** The description says the
dropped `</think>` affects *both* streaming and non-streaming responses, but the test
added with the fix only drives `extract_tool_calls`. The streaming counterpart is now
covered by `test_streaming_closing_think_end_in_content_is_preserved`, which uses the
repo's own `simulate_tool_streaming` helper: `<think>` opens reasoning, the first
`</think>` closes it, and the second one sits in content, where it is data rather than a
boundary. Both cases fail against the previous config — `(CONTENT, "THINK_END")`
emitting no events — and pass with it, so the streaming half of the claim is measured
rather than assumed. The file is 16 passed.

**The follow-up commit contains no product change**: it adds one test, so a review of
`e769f90` still applies as-is.

**Patch coverage could not be measured on this box.** `pytest --cov` fails here (torch
under coverage's import instrumentation), and `coverage run` on this target dumps core;
the same tooling fails across this PR series for the same class of reason. The
behavioural evidence is stronger than a percentage in this case: the changed line is a
single value in the `minimax_m2_config()` transition table, every test builds the engine
from that config, and the two cases above fail without the change and pass with it —
which can only happen if the changed line is active.

**Cross-config / cross-provider.** Seven parser configs define a
`(CONTENT, "THINK_END")` transition — `kimi_k2`, `qwen3`, `mistral`, `glm47_moe`,
`deepseek_v4`, `gemma4` and this one — and the other six keep `()`, i.e. they still
consume a `</think>` seen in the content state. That is deliberate and correct for them:
none of them has an append-think mode, so a `</think>` in content there is a stray
delimiter rather than data. `grep append_think` finds only `vllm/parser/minimax_m2.py`
plus the reasoning-parser registry, so the change is confined to the config that needs
it. The shared engine is untouched — `TEXT_CHUNK` is an existing event type that other
transitions already emit — and the normal `minimax_m2` reasoning path still has its
boundary owned by the `(REASONING, "THINK_END")` transition; the changed transition only
matches a `</think>` reached while already in `CONTENT`, which is the append-think case.
The file's pre-existing reasoning and streaming cases still pass.

items.title: [Bugfix] Reserve max-num-queued-reqs slots at preflight so a burst is rejected before render
items.body:
## Summary

`--max-num-queued-reqs` was checked twice per request — once as a preflight
(`check_admission(n)`, no `request_id`) before render, and once at hand-over
(`check_admission(request_id=...)`) after render — but nothing was counted
between the two. Under a burst, every request passed the preflight, the
single-worker multimodal renderer then rendered them one at a time, and the
surplus was rejected with `QueueOverflowError` (HTTP 503) only after paying
the full render cost. This change makes the preflight **reserve** the slots it
checks, so requests that will be refused are refused up front instead of after
rendering.

## Problem

Reported in #58192:

- `check_admission(n)` (preflight) is called from `GenerateBaseServing._preflight`
  before `online_renderer.render_*`.
- `check_admission(request_id=...)` is called again in `AsyncLLM._add_request`
  / the `n>1` fan-out, after `input_processor.process_inputs_async` (the render).

Both reads only see requests already handed over to the `OutputProcessor`.
A request in between the two checks is invisible to admission. In a production
burst the API server held ~85–101 requests in the render pipeline while the
engine itself was empty, and 54% of the 503s took 4–9 s p50 to arrive because
the request had already been fetched and rendered.

## Root cause

The preflight check and the hand-over check observe the same counter
(`get_num_unfinished_requests()`) at two different times, with an unbounded
render in between. There is no bookkeeping for "admitted, not yet handed over."

## Solution

Add a per-process reservation ledger to `AsyncLLM`:

- The **preflight** call (`request_id is None`) now also reserves `n` slots
  when it passes, so `unfinished + reserved` is the live admission count.
- The **hand-over** call (`request_id` given) consumes `n` reserved slots — the
  request moves from `reserved` to `unfinished` rather than being double counted.
- A 60 s TTL ages out reservations whose request never hands over (client
  disconnect during render, render error), so a dropped connection cannot leak
  a slot forever.

The second check becomes a backstop by construction: at preflight we already
guarantee `unfinished + reserved + n <= max`, and hand-over only transfers a
slot.

## Testing

New unit tests in `tests/v1/engine/test_admission_control.py`:

- `test_preflight_reserves_slots_and_bounds_a_burst`
- `test_handover_consumes_preflight_reservation`
- `test_abandoned_preflight_reservation_times_out`
- `test_preflight_reservation_is_n_aware`

All existing admission tests are unchanged in expectation and pass (the
`__new__`-based test harness now seeds the new reservation state).

## Compatibility

- No API or config changes. `max_num_queued_reqs` now actually bounds what it
  says: requests are rejected at preflight rather than after render.
- The reservation counter is per-process. The shared `SharedAdmissionStats`
  (used with `--api-server-count > 1`) is still aggregated at hand-over exactly
  as before; this only closes the single-process render gap.
- Behavior for `max_num_queued_tokens` is unchanged.

## Related

Fixes #58192.

## Readiness gate

Run at head `eb263a6` on a CPU-only box (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`).

**Tests.** `tests/v1/engine/test_admission_control.py` is **54 passed**, including the four
cases added here: reserve-and-bound-a-burst, hand-over-consumes-the-reservation, the TTL
expiry of an abandoned reservation, and the n-aware path.

**Patch coverage could not be measured on this box.** `pytest --cov` fails on every vLLM
target here (torch under coverage's import instrumentation), and `coverage run
--source=vllm.v1.engine.async_llm` **dumps core** on this file, so no figure is quoted
rather than a misleading one. The behavioural evidence is what the gate rests on: the
tests above fail without the reservation logic (the burst case is exactly the behaviour
that did not exist before) and pass with it.

**Edge-case review.** The change adds three things — a `deque` of reservation timestamps,
a `threading.Lock` around the check, and a TTL purge — so the cases that matter are the
state transitions and the ordering assumption, not arithmetic:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| burst of preflights at the cap | 10 reserve, the 11th raises `QueueOverflowError` before render |
| hand-over after preflight | reservation consumed, slot moves from `reserved` to `unfinished`, no double count |
| abandoned reservation (client died during render) | purged once older than `_ADMISSION_RESERVATION_TTL_S` (60 s) |
| `n > 1` fan-out | preflight reserves `n`, hand-over consumes `min(n, reserved)` |
| purge ordering assumption | all `n` slots of one reservation share one `time.monotonic()` value and are appended together, so FIFO order is time order — the leftmost entry really is the oldest |
| lock held across an `await` | no: the critical section is pure `deque` operations, so the `threading.Lock` cannot block the event loop |

**The one thing worth checking was whether a hand-over can consume a reservation it never
made**, which would silently free another request's slot. Traced through the callers, and
it cannot: every HTTP entrypoint preflights — `_preflight` (`generate/base/serving.py:174`)
is called by `openai/chat_completion/serving.py:240`, `openai/completion/serving.py:105`,
`openai/responses/serving.py:335`, `openai/chat_completion/batch_serving.py:60`,
`speech_to_text/base/serving.py:442` and `scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py:119`,
and `generate/generative_scoring/serving.py:204` calls `check_admission` directly. The one
path that reaches `add_request` without preflighting is the offline `LLM`
(`entrypoints/offline_utils.py:573`), and it cannot steal anything because nothing on that
path ever reserves — `_admission_reserved` stays empty, so `min(n, reserved)` is zero. The
reservation logic is also skipped entirely while `max_num_queued_reqs` is `None`, which is
its default (`config/scheduler.py:87`).

**Residual risks, stated rather than hidden.** Two are inherent to the design: the 60 s TTL
means a legitimate render that takes longer than that lets its slot be reused, so the cap
can be exceeded by the number of such in-flight renders (bounded, and the alternative is a
permanent leak); and reservations are anonymous timestamps, so a hand-over consumes the
*oldest* reservation rather than "its own" — equivalent for a count, but it means a TTL
expiry can belong to a different request than the one that leaked.

**Cross-backend.** The change is in the engine's admission path — pure Python, no device
code, so CUDA / ROCm / NPU / MUSA / CPU are unaffected. `check_admission` also exists as a
no-op default on the `EngineClient` protocol (`engine/protocol.py:71`), so other engine
client implementations keep their existing behaviour.
