`--max-num-queued-reqs` was checked twice per request — once as a preflight
(`check_admission(n)`, no `request_id`) before render, and once at hand-over
(`check_admission(request_id=...)`) after render — but nothing was counted
between the two. Under a burst, every request passed the preflight, the
single-worker multimodal renderer then rendered them one at a time, and the
surplus was rejected with `QueueOverflowError` (HTTP 503) only after paying
the full render cost. This change makes the preflight **reserve** the slots it
checks, so requests that will be refused are refused up front instead of after
rendering.

## Problem

Reported in #58192:

- `check_admission(n)` (preflight) is called from `GenerateBaseServing._preflight`
  before `online_renderer.render_*`.
- `check_admission(request_id=...)` is called again in `AsyncLLM._add_request`
  / the `n>1` fan-out, after `input_processor.process_inputs_async` (the render).

Both reads only see requests already handed over to the `OutputProcessor`.
A request in between the two checks is invisible to admission. In a production
burst the API server held ~85–101 requests in the render pipeline while the
engine itself was empty, and 54% of the 503s took 4–9 s p50 to arrive because
the request had already been fetched and rendered.

## Root cause

The preflight check and the hand-over check observe the same counter
(`get_num_unfinished_requests()`) at two different times, with an unbounded
render in between. There is no bookkeeping for "admitted, not yet handed over."

## Solution

Add a per-process reservation ledger to `AsyncLLM`:

- The **preflight** call (`request_id is None`) now also reserves `n` slots
  when it passes, so `unfinished + reserved` is the live admission count.
- The **hand-over** call (`request_id` given) consumes `n` reserved slots — the
  request moves from `reserved` to `unfinished` rather than being double counted.
- A 60 s TTL ages out reservations whose request never hands over (client
  disconnect during render, render error), so a dropped connection cannot leak
  a slot forever.

The second check becomes a backstop by construction: at preflight we already
guarantee `unfinished + reserved + n <= max`, and hand-over only transfers a
slot.

## Testing

New unit tests in `tests/v1/engine/test_admission_control.py`:

- `test_preflight_reserves_slots_and_bounds_a_burst`
- `test_handover_consumes_preflight_reservation`
- `test_abandoned_preflight_reservation_times_out`
- `test_preflight_reservation_is_n_aware`

All existing admission tests are unchanged in expectation and pass (the
`__new__`-based test harness now seeds the new reservation state).

## Compatibility

- No API or config changes. `max_num_queued_reqs` now actually bounds what it
  says: requests are rejected at preflight rather than after render.
- The reservation counter is per-process. The shared `SharedAdmissionStats`
  (used with `--api-server-count > 1`) is still aggregated at hand-over exactly
  as before; this only closes the single-process render gap.
- Behavior for `max_num_queued_tokens` is unchanged.

## Related

Fixes #58192.

items.title: [Bugfix][Reasoning] Handle multi-token streaming deltas in the Hunyuan A13B parser
items.body:
## Purpose

Fix a crash (and silent output loss under `python -O`) in streaming responses
when `--reasoning-parser hunyuan_a13b` is used together with any feature that
emits more than one token per generation step (speculative decoding, MTP).

No issue was filed for this; it appeared while auditing the streaming paths of
every reasoning parser for unhandled input shapes. Happy to file one if you
prefer that as the tracking entry.

## Problem

`HunyuanA13BReasoningParser.extract_reasoning_streaming()` assumed one token per
streaming delta:

```python
assert len(delta_token_ids) == 1
# Process each token in the delta
token = delta_token_ids[0]
```

The engine calls the parser once per generation step and passes the step's token
ids:

```python
# vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py
delta_message = parser.parse_delta(
    delta_text=delta_text,
    delta_token_ids=as_list(output.token_ids),
    ...
)
```

A step carries several tokens when speculative decoding or MTP is enabled, so
`len(delta_token_ids) > 1` reaches the parser and the assertion fires:

```
AssertionError
```

That surfaces as a failed request / broken stream. With `python -O` the
assertion is compiled out instead, and the parser processes only
`delta_token_ids[0]` while `delta_text` still describes the whole delta — so the
remaining tokens are silently dropped from the response.

Reproduced by driving the parser directly, feeding the same token ids in slices:

```
before:  delta size  1: reasoning= 11 content=  7  ok
         delta size  2: reasoning=  0 content=  0  AssertionError
         delta size  5: reasoning=  0 content=  0  AssertionError
after:   delta size  1: reasoning= 11 content=  7  ok
         delta size  2: reasoning= 11 content=  7  ok
         delta size  5: reasoning= 11 content=  7  ok
```

## Solution

Iterate the delta's tokens through the existing per-token state machine and
combine the emitted parts into one `DeltaMessage` (or `None` when nothing is
emitted, as before).

- Per-token text is decoded from the token ids when a delta holds more than one
  token, following the convention already used elsewhere in the tree
  (`MiniMaxM3ReasoningParser._decode_text` decodes token ids the same way).
- A single-token delta keeps using the engine's `delta_text` unchanged, so
  existing behaviour is preserved exactly.
- Empty deltas return `None` early.

This matches how the rest of the codebase treats deltas: `basic_parsers`,
`ernie45`, `hy_v4` and `step3` guard with `len(delta_token_ids) == 1` before a
single-token shortcut, `minimax_m3` iterates every token, and
`deepseekv3_tool_parser` / `deepseekv31_tool_parser` have explicit
`len(delta_token_ids) > 1` branches.

## Testing

```
HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu \
  pytest tests/reasoning/test_hunyuan_reasoning_parser.py -q
```

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| New test only, with the fix | **4 passed** (delta sizes 2, 3, 7, 100) |
| Whole file, with the fix | **21 passed** (existing 17 + new 4) |
| New test only, fix reverted | **4 failed** — the test does catch the defect |
| `ruff check` / `ruff format` | clean |

The regression test builds the token id stream from the parser's own marker ids
(`think_start_ids` / `response_start_ids` / `response_end_ids`) plus a payload,
then requires that feeding the ids in slices of N produces exactly the same
output as feeding them one at a time. The existing tests in that file drive the
streaming path one token at a time, which is why this was never caught.

## Compatibility

No behaviour change for single-token deltas, which is what the parser was
written for. Multi-token deltas previously raised; they now produce the same
output as the equivalent sequence of single-token calls.

## AI assistance disclosure

The investigation, patch and test in this PR were produced with AI tooling
(DeepSeek Harness). I reviewed every changed line, reproduced the failure and
the fix locally, and ran the tests listed above.

---

**Duplicate check (required before writing code).**

Two other PRs touch `hunyuan_a13b_reasoning_parser.py`; both were read before
concluding this one is not a duplicate:

- **#58130** (cs-fisha, 2026-09-22) fixes the *other* Hunyuan streaming defect — the
  closing `\n</answer>` leaking into content once `DelegatingParser` declares reasoning
  over. It does that by adding an opt-in `post_reasoning_stream_filter` to the shared
  `DelegatingParser` in `vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py`, keeping post-reasoning deltas
  on the Hunyuan state machine. It does **not** touch delta tokenisation, so it does not
  cover this PR.
- **#58521** in this repository is ours and fixes exactly that `</answer>` leak
  detector-locally, i.e. it overlaps #58130's defect rather than this one. It is the one
  that should be dropped if #58130 lands, not this.

What this PR is for: `parse_delta` asserted one token per delta and read
`delta_token_ids[0]`, so a multi-token delta (speculative decoding / MTP, or
`stream_interval > 1`) either tripped the assert or mis-decoded the step. The fix
iterates the delta token-by-token and decodes each token's own text. No open PR from
anyone else addresses that.

## Readiness gate

Run against the follow-up commit `5211929` on a CPU-only box (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`).

**Patch coverage.** 100% of the changed lines of
`hunyuan_a13b_reasoning_parser.py` (47 lines, 0 missing) under
`pytest tests/reasoning/test_hunyuan_reasoning_parser.py`; the file as a whole
reports 94%, and every remaining miss is a pre-existing line.

Tooling note, in case anyone hits it: `pytest --cov` is unusable on this box —
importing `torch` under coverage tracing raises `SystemError: ... method: bad call
flags`, in both the vLLM and the other venv, with the default tracer and with
`COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`/`pytrace`. Running pytest *under*
`coverage run --rcfile=.coveragerc` works, and that is what produced these numbers.

**Edge cases.**

| input | result |
|---|---|
| empty delta (`delta_token_ids=[]`) | returns `None`; was uncovered, now tested |
| single token | unchanged, still uses the engine's `delta_text` |
| multi-token, ASCII | identical to the single-token feed at steps 2/3/7/100 |
| multi-token, byte-fallback boundary (emoji) | **was corrupt** — see below |
| delta longer than `current_token_ids` | no crash |
| malformed input | no exception raised on any row |

The byte-boundary row was a real defect in this PR's own new code.
`_iter_delta_tokens` derived each token's text as `cur_text[len(prev_text):]`, which
assumes `decode(ids[:n])` is a prefix of `decode(ids[:n+1])`. Token 222 of
`tencent/Hunyuan-A13B-Instruct` is the second fragment of 🚀, and the prefix
relation breaks exactly there:

```
decode(ids[:4]) ends '... rocket \ufffd'
decode(ids[:5]) ends '... rocket 🚀'
```

so the slice took the wrong text and an emoji in reasoning content came out as
`\ufffd`. Text ending in `\ufffd` is now withheld until the character completes —
the guard `detokenize_incrementally` already applies
(`vllm/tokenizers/detokenizer_utils.py:261`). `test_per_token_text_reconstructs_the_delta`
fails on the two astral payloads without that change, and `test_empty_delta_returns_none`
covers the branch the coverage run flagged.

Verified: 27 passed for the file (21 before), `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`
clean. An emoji payload cannot be asserted through the streaming-equivalence test —
its harness derives `delta_text` as `tokenizer.decode(delta)`, which is lossy for a
slice that ends mid-character — so the astral case is asserted against the helper
directly instead.

**Cross-provider / backend.** `_iter_delta_tokens` is private to this detector and
called only from `extract_reasoning_streaming`, so no sibling inherits it: the other
parsers override `extract_reasoning_streaming` themselves and the shared base is
untouched. Both streaming entrypoints pass multi-token deltas —
`chat_completion/serving.py:659` and `responses/serving.py:1220-1225` both use
`as_list(output.token_ids)` — and the parser framework forwards `delta_token_ids` at
`abstract_parser.py:715`, which is also where an empty delta can arrive. The change
is pure Python: no kernels and no device code, so CUDA / ROCm / NPU / MUSA / CPU are
unaffected.

items.title: [Bugfix] Deep-merge nested mm_processor_kwargs so request overrides do not drop configured keys
items.body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #58406. This PR fixes the concrete data-loss half of the reported `mm_processor_kwargs` issue: the shallow merge replaced whole nested mappings and silently dropped configured keys.

## Problem

`MultiModalConfig.merge_mm_processor_kwargs` combined configured and request kwargs with a shallow dict union (`kwargs | dict(inference_kwargs)`). When both sides supply a nested mapping — e.g. configured `videos_kwargs={"fps": 2, "size": {...}}` and request `videos_kwargs={"size": {...}}` — the request's dict wholesale replaces the configured one, dropping `fps` (and any other key not repeated in the request).

Reproduced from the issue:

```python
config = MultiModalConfig(mm_processor_kwargs={
    "size": {"shortest_edge": 100, "longest_edge": 1000},
    "videos_kwargs": {"fps": 2, "size": {"longest_edge": 1200}},
})
merged = config.merge_mm_processor_kwargs({
    "size": {"longest_edge": 1800},
    "videos_kwargs": {"size": {"shortest_edge": 200}},
})
# Before: merged["videos_kwargs"] == {"size": {"shortest_edge": 200}}  (fps lost)
# After:  merged["videos_kwargs"] == {"fps": 2, "size": {"longest_edge": 1200, "shortest_edge": 200}}
```

## Solution

Add `_deep_merge_mm_kwargs`, which recursively merges nested `Mapping` values key-by-key while leaving non-mapping override behavior unchanged (request wins on leaf values, new keys are added, a non-mapping request value still replaces a configured mapping). This is backward compatible: flat kwargs continue to override exactly as before, and no behavior changes for requests that do not send nested mappings.

The flat-vs-scoped precedence contract (engine flat < engine scoped < request flat < request scoped) described in the issue is a larger design change to the overlay path and is intentionally left for a follow-up; this PR only stops the silent data loss.

## Test Plan

Added `test_mm_processor_kwargs_deep_merges_nested_scoped_kwargs` in `tests/multimodal/test_processing.py`, covering the issue's repro: configured `fps` survives, and nested `size` dicts merge key-by-key.

## Test Result

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both files.
- A standalone equivalent of the merge function reproduces the regression (fps dropped before) and confirms the merged result after, plus flat-override, new-key, and mapping-replaced-by-scalar cases.

## Compatibility

No API change. Requests that previously sent nested kwargs will now retain configured sibling keys instead of dropping them, which is the intended behavior; requests without nested kwargs are unaffected.

## Related Issue

Relates to #58406.

items.title: [Bugfix] Stop re-forcing thinking-budget end tokens once the forced end sequence is complete
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58390.

When `thinking_token_budget` is exhausted, the Model Runner V2 thinking-budget kernel (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/thinking_budget.py`) forces the model to walk out of the reasoning section by writing `1e9` onto the next token in `reasoning_end_token_ids`. With reasoning configs whose forced end sequence does not coincide with a natural-reasoning-end marker (e.g. distinct `reasoning_end_token_ids` / `natural_reasoning_end_token_ids`), the kernel never stops forcing after the walk completes and the request collapses into a repetition loop the moment the boundary is reached.

## Problem

The kernel advances the forced walk by measuring how long a prefix of `reasoning_end_token_ids` already matches the tail (`end_prefix_len`) and forcing `reasoning_end_token_ids[end_prefix_len + 1]`. The only thing that stops forcing is the natural-end early return (`last_start <= last_end`), which relies on a `natural_reasoning_end_token_ids` marker actually appearing in the sequence.

Once the *complete* forced end sequence is in the tail, the prefix alignment shifts: e.g. tail `[END_A, END_B]` no longer matches `prefix_len=1` against `END_A`, so `end_prefix_len` is recomputed as `0` and the kernel re-forces `END_A` again. On the next step the tail is `[END_B, END_A]`, which matches `END_A` and forces `END_B` again, and so on forever. For configs where the forced end tokens are not also natural-end tokens, `last_start <= last_end` never becomes true, so the loop only ends when the sampler's repetition guard trips (observed as ~`min_pattern_size * min_count` = 64 repeated tokens after the boundary).

## Root Cause

Missing "walk already complete" guard in `_thinking_budget_kernel`. The prefix-match loop only ever tests prefix lengths `1..END_LEN-1`, so it cannot recognize that the tail already contains the whole sequence. It therefore has no way to release forcing after the exit walk finishes.

## Solution

Before writing the forced logit, check whether the tail already ends with the *complete* `reasoning_end_token_ids` sequence. If so, return without forcing so the model can resume normal generation. This is safe:

- If the forced end tokens also coincide with natural-end tokens, the existing `last_start <= last_end` return already stops forcing; the new guard is redundant but harmless.
- It only triggers when the whole exit sequence is present, so it cannot cut a multi-token walk short mid-way (partial prefixes are still forced as before).
- A later reasoning re-entry (a new start marker) updates `last_start` and forcing resumes as expected.

## Test Plan

Added `test_v2_thinking_budget_stops_after_forced_end_sequence_complete` to `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py`: with a distinct forced/natural-end config, after the full `[END_A, END_B]` sequence is committed, the next decode row must receive no `1e9` logit.

Existing tests still encode the intended walk:
- `test_v2_thinking_budget_continues_multi_token_end_marker` forces `END_A` then `END_B`.
- `test_v2_thinking_budget_uses_distinct_forced_end_marker` exercises the distinct config mid-walk.

## Test Result

- Ruff: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both changed files.
- A CPU equivalent of the kernel decision logic (prefix match + force, with and without the new guard) reproduces the regression: the buggy path re-forces `END_A` after the complete sequence, the patched path returns without forcing, and the single-token-end and partial-prefix walk cases are unchanged.
- The new GPU test is skipped on CPU runners (`pytest.importorskip("triton")` / `torch.cuda.is_available()` guard, consistent with the rest of the file) and will run in CI.

## Compatibility

No API or config change. Behavior only changes for requests that previously hung in a repetition loop after `thinking_token_budget` was exhausted under a distinct forced/natural-end reasoning config; such requests now leave the reasoning section and continue generating.

## Related Issue

Fixes #58390.

---

## AI assistance disclosure

This PR was prepared with AI tooling (Claude Code) under human direction. The author has reviewed every changed line and run the tests listed above.

items.title: [Bugfix] Re-anchor promoted partial prefix-cache entries on the surviving block-aligned ancestor
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58394.

When an existing partial prefix-cache entry is **promoted** to a later boundary
(`BlockPool.cache_partial_block()`), the same call emits:

1. a `BlockRemoved` event for the previous partial boundary, and
2. a `BlockStored` event for the new boundary whose `parent_block_hash` is that
   just-removed hash.

External KV-cache event consumers (gateways / connectors that rebuild the prefix
chain from the event stream) therefore receive a dangling parent reference: the
only event naming that hash in the same batch says it was removed, so the chain
cannot be walked without cross-batch state.

## Root Cause

The natural parent of a promoted boundary is exactly the previous partial
boundary — the two boundaries are adjacent `hash_block_size` steps apart. On
promotion the previous boundary is removed *and* named as the parent in the same
event batch.

## Solution

On promotion, re-anchor the new entry on the last **block-aligned** ancestor
(the owning block's start) instead of the boundary being removed:

- `parent_block_hash` = the hash chain at the owning block boundary, which was
  emitted as a stored full block in an earlier batch and is never removed here.
- the `BlockStored` span widens from `[previous_boundary, num_tokens)` to
  `[block_start, num_tokens)`, so the entry genuinely covers the span its parent
  implies.

The first-registration path (block has no prior hash) is untouched — that case
already reports a never-removed parent and is pinned by
`test_cache_partial_block_kv_cache_events`.

For the repro in #58394 (`hash_block_size=2`, `block_size=6`, promote 8 → 10):
the batch is now `BlockRemoved(H8)` + `BlockStored(H10, parent=H6,
token_ids[6:10], block_size=4)`, self-contained exactly as
`BlockRemoved` + `BlockStored(parent=<hash never removed>)` requires.

## Test Plan

- Updated `test_partial_block_replacement_emits_remove_then_store_events` to pin
  the promoted-parent contract: the stored parent must be the surviving
  block-aligned boundary (6-token) rather than the removed 8-token boundary, the
  span must be `[6:10)`, and `block_size` is the widened span length.
- No wire-format change: `BlockStored`/`BlockRemoved` schemas are unchanged, so
  `tests/distributed/test_kv_cache_events.py` keeps passing.
- Local stub replay of the real `cache_partial_block()` (AST-extracted from this
  patch) confirms:
  - first registration unchanged: `Stored(H8, parent=H6, [6:8))`;
  - promotion batch: `Removed(H8)` then `Stored(H10, parent=H6, [6:10), size=4)`
    with the parent not equal to any removed hash;
  - multi-block case (`block_size=12`, promote 16 → 20) re-anchors at block
    boundary 12.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.

## Test Result

- `pytest tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_primitives.py`:
  existing suite passes with the updated assertions (17 tests).
- `tests/distributed/test_kv_cache_events.py`: wire-format tests unaffected.
- No runtime/CUDA behavior change — only KV-cache *event* metadata emitted on
  the promotion path; the in-memory prefix-cache keys (`H8` removed, `H10`
  inserted) are unchanged.

---

**Duplicate check (required before writing code).**

Closest open PR: **#58121** (draft, Lucas-Fernandes-Martins) — `[Core][KV Events] Emit
skipped ancestry for partial cache events` — which shares `block_pool.py`. It is a draft
stacked on #44488 about which ancestor hash a `BlockStored` event reports; this PR is about
re-anchoring a **promoted** partial entry onto the surviving block so a stale parent hash
is not referenced. Related area, different mechanism.

I contributed a measurement to #58121 (the `BlockStored` payload moving 221 → 223 bytes
when a field is added), so I am aware of its scope and not working against it. If it lands
first and covers this case, I will close this; if the reverse, the note there can point
here.

## Readiness gate

Run on a CPU-only box (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`), rebased onto main `3b4566c` (the branch is now two commits: the fix, then the multimodal regression test).

**Patch coverage.** 100% of the `block_pool.py` delta (17 lines, 0 missing) under
`pytest tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_primitives.py`; the module
as a whole reports 71%, and every remaining miss is a pre-existing line.

**Edge cases.** Six rows, all passing:

| input | result |
|---|---|
| first block of the request (`block_start == 0`) | parent is `None`, on both the promotion and the replace path |
| promoted across a block boundary | re-anchored to the block-aligned ancestor; no removed parent |
| `num_tokens` an exact multiple of `block_size` | no crash; natural parent, which is not removed |
| `block_size == hash_block_size` | unreachable — every hash boundary is then a block boundary, so the pre-existing asserts at `block_pool.py:494-497` and `:580` reject it; no new branch lives there |
| non-zero `kv_cache_group_id` | group preserved on both the removed and stored event |
| malformed input | no exception raised on any row |

**The defect this gate found, and the fix.** The removed-parent guard only covered the
branch that *promotes* a partial entry. Reusing a block with
`replace_existing_hashes=True` — which is what `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:2064`
does when it re-keys a Mamba checkpoint block — also removes the block's previous
hashes in the same batch, and the removed hash can be exactly the boundary the new
partial entry would name as its parent. Reproduced at unit level before the change:

```
BlockRemoved   [hash@8]
BlockStored    parent_block_hash = hash@8      <- the batch removes the parent it names
```

The decision now depends on the actual condition — whether the hash about to be named
as the parent is in this batch's removed set — rather than only on the promotion flag.
That covers both branches and leaves the promotion case unchanged.
`test_replaced_block_does_not_name_a_removed_parent` fails without the change and
passes with it. The file is 15 passed; `ruff check` passes and `ruff format --check`
reports both files already formatted.

**Cross-provider / backend.** One subclass inherits `cache_partial_block`
(`SharedEventQueueBlockPool`, `vllm/v1/hisparse/block_pool.py:8`), and all three callers
live in `vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` (lines 883, 2064, 2107). The
change affects only KV-cache **event metadata**, so the readers to re-check are
`vllm/distributed/kv_events.py:58`,
`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/events.py`,
`.../v1/mooncake/store/worker.py`, `.../v1/lmcache_connector.py:247` and
`vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py`. The change is pure Python — no kernels and no
device code — so CUDA / ROCm / NPU / MUSA / CPU are unaffected.

Tooling note, as on #58412: `pytest --cov` cannot run on this box, because importing
`torch` under coverage tracing raises `SystemError: ... method: bad call flags`. Running
pytest *under* `coverage run --rcfile=.coveragerc` works, and that is what produced the
numbers above.

---

## Verified against current main

*Rebased onto main `3b4566c` on 2026-09-26 (the branch previously carried three commits from `9ef37771`; it is now two commits on current main).*

Main changed this same function after the PR branched: `f6aa2919` — "[Bugfix][Core] Keep every
multimodal feature in the partial-block KV event" (#58288) — added `get_mm_features_in_window`
to `cache_partial_block` and extended this same test file, so **both** files this PR touches
have moved since `9ef37771`. Re-checked against main `3b4566c`:

- **Both files merge cleanly.** A per-file three-way merge with this PR's base as the merge
  base leaves no conflict in `vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py` or the test file.
- **The two changes compose in the right order.** This PR re-anchors `parent_hash` and
  `block_start` *before* `extra_keys` is derived, so the new `curr_mm_idx` logic reads the
  re-anchored `block_start` and describes the span the entry actually stores. Measuring the
  re-anchor path with a multimodal placeholder covering tokens `[6, 8)` (inside the widened
  span `[6, 10)`, outside the un-re-anchored `[8, 10)`):

  | | `token_ids` | `block_size` | `extra_keys` |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | main alone | `[4, 4]` (span `[8, 10)`) | 2 | `[None]` |
  | main + this PR | `[3, 3, 4, 4]` (span `[6, 10)`) | 4 | `[(('A', 0),)]` |

  The feature reaching into the widened part of the span is reported, which is what the
  widened entry requires; deriving the window *before* the re-anchor would drop it and let
  two requests with different multimodal content publish the same key.

- **`pytest tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_primitives.py`**: all 16
  collected items in the file pass against main's logic plus this change, including the new
  `test_cache_partial_block_event_keeps_every_mm_feature`.
- **Control**: `test_replaced_block_does_not_name_a_removed_parent` fails against unmodified
  main's source, so it still pins the defect rather than passing vacuously.

**The gap above is now closed.** The branch is rebased onto `3b4566c`, and `test_reanchored_partial_block_reports_the_widened_mm_window` covers exactly this combination in the committed test file. It fails against unmodified main's `block_pool.py` and passes with the change, so the ordering the two blocks depend on is now pinned by a test rather than by a measurement I ran once.

items.title: [Bugfix][V1][AsyncScheduler] Clamp delivered tokens to reserved output placeholders instead of killing EngineCore
items.body:
## Summary

`AsyncScheduler._update_request_with_output` assumes the model runner never returns more tokens than the scheduler reserved output placeholders for. When it does, `num_output_placeholders -= len(new_token_ids)` goes negative, the invariant `assert request.num_output_placeholders >= 0` fires, and EngineCore is killed -- taking the whole engine down with every connected client.

This PR clamps the delivered tokens to the number actually reserved and logs a warning, so an over-delivery degrades into a dropped token plus a visible diagnostic instead of a process kill.

**Scope, stated plainly:** this is a defensive guard on the delivery side, not a fix for the underlying disagreement between the scheduler's reservation predicate and the model runner's discard predicate. That disagreement is the real bug and lives on both sides of the scheduler/worker boundary. This PR does not attempt to resolve it; it makes it survivable and observable.

## Status of the triggers that motivated this PR (updated 2026-09-30)

The description previously carried the framing, from @yeighta's 2026-09-24 comment, that for the #57562 trigger the clamp is "not a backstop -- right now it is the only thing between the divergence and a dead engine." **That is no longer true and has been removed.**

The divergence on the reporting machine comes from the V2 model runner reading stale UVA buffers under Confidential Computing. It is now **fixed at the source** by [#57404](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57404) or [#57415](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57415). With either applied, the same 12-request chunked-prefill repro completes with no underflow at all, so the clamp is never reached. **For the CC trigger the clamp is a defensive backstop again, not the only thing preventing a dead engine.** The measurements are in [Hardware validation](#hardware-validation).

The same is true of the second trigger this PR was argued to cover, the resumable-request path from #50692: it is fixed at source on `main` by #58259, and does not reproduce there any more -- see [Trigger 2](#trigger-2-the-resumable-request-path-50692).

**What the guard is still for.** Both triggers that motivated this PR have since been fixed at their source, which is the outcome we wanted. What is left is the invariant itself: `assert request.num_output_placeholders >= 0` is still fatal to the engine, and nothing anywhere asserts that the scheduler's reservation predicate and the runner's discard predicate agree. This PR's own synthetic trigger still reproduces on current `main` (measured, see [Testing](#testing)), and the `/v1/realtime` over-commit described in #30142 is a third instance that is not fixed at source. The guard makes that whole class non-fatal and observable instead of a process kill, which is the reason to keep it even though it is no longer load-bearing for either original trigger.

Fixes #57562

## Problem

With chunked prefill + concurrency, no spec decode and no preemption:

```
vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py:63: AssertionError
        request.num_output_placeholders -= len(new_token_ids)
>       assert request.num_output_placeholders >= 0
```

Counters captured at the crash:

```
placeholders=-1 new_tokens=1 computed=8448 num_tokens=9119
prompt=9118 output=1 in_flight=1056 prefill_chunk=True status=RUNNING
```

From the report:
- `--no-async-scheduling` -> 24/24 requests pass; chunked prompts -> 44 underflows; single-chunk prompts -> 0.
- Spurious tokens reach the response while the request is still prefilling.

## Mechanism

The same subtraction is implicated in the wider `num_output_placeholders` family, tracked in #30142. From @amanchugh89's analysis there:

> `_update_after_schedule` reserves a fixed `1 + cur_num_spec_tokens` per scheduled step, but the `/v1/realtime` decode can commit more than that for a single step, so `num_output_placeholders -= len(new_token_ids)` drives the counter below zero and the assert fires.

In #57562 the delivery is *smaller* than the reservation but the reservation is **zero**: the request is a prefill chunk, for which `_update_after_schedule` reserves nothing:

```python
for req_id in scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens:
    request = self.requests[req_id]
    if request.is_prefill_chunk:
        continue
    ...
    request.num_output_placeholders += (
        self.num_sampled_tokens_per_step + cur_num_spec_tokens
    )
```

where

```python
request.is_prefill_chunk = request.num_computed_tokens < (
    request.num_tokens + request.num_output_placeholders
)
```

Both triggers are the same shape: **`len(new_token_ids) > request.num_output_placeholders`**. The clamp below covers both; nothing in it is specific to chunked prefill.

The scheduler's expectation that the runner returns no token for a chunk request is documented as a contract in the parent class:

```python
# Note that if a request is still being prefilled, we expect the model
# runner to return empty token ids for the request.
```

The runner enforces its own copy of that predicate, from a different formula and against worker-side state (`GPUModelRunner`):

```python
self.optimistic_seq_lens_cpu[:num_reqs] = (
    self.input_batch.num_computed_tokens_cpu_tensor[:num_reqs]
    + num_scheduled_tokens
)
...
num_tokens = [self.requests[r].num_tokens for r in self.input_batch.req_ids]
self.discard_request_mask.np[:num_reqs] = (
    self.optimistic_seq_lens_cpu[:num_reqs].numpy() < num_tokens_np
)
```

So the two sides each decide "is this request still prefilling?" from local state:

| | predicate | state it reads |
|---|---|---|
| scheduler (reserve) | `computed < num_tokens + num_output_placeholders` | scheduler's `Request` |
| runner (discard) | `computed + scheduled < num_tokens` | worker's mirrored `Request` |

They are expected to agree -- the scheduler adds `num_output_placeholders` precisely to account for tokens that exist on the worker but have not been delivered back yet -- but nothing asserts it, and they can disagree.

A hardware measurement settled which side introduces the divergence for this trigger. Under the identical load on the same machine, the V2 model runner produces 42 underflows and the V1 runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) produces **zero**. The scheduler and the reservation predicate above are unchanged between those two runs, so here the over-delivery is produced on the runner side. The follow-up measurement identified the mechanism: under CC, `pin_memory=True` does not actually pin (`is_pinned()` returns `False`), and the device view is not a live alias of host memory, so the runner reads stale buffers. [#57404](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57404) makes `is_uva_available()` fail closed when the alias is not live; [#57415](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57415) disables UVA under CC outright. Either removes the divergence at its source. This does not change the guard -- it covers over-delivery whichever side produces it -- but it is where the underlying fix belongs.

## Solution

Clamp the delivered tokens to the number of placeholders actually reserved, and warn:

```python
def _update_request_with_output(
    self, request: Request, new_token_ids: list[int], is_stale: bool = False
) -> tuple[list[int], bool]:
    status_before_update = request.status

    if not is_stale and len(new_token_ids) > request.num_output_placeholders:
        # The runner may only return tokens for steps that the scheduler
        # reserved output placeholders for, and must return none while a
        # request is still being prefilled. If it returns one anyway, that
        # token was sampled from an incomplete prefix and is not a valid
        # continuation: drop it rather than appending garbage to the
        # response and driving num_output_placeholders negative, which trips
        # the invariant below and kills EngineCore.
        #
        # Dropping is a correctness fix, not only crash protection: without
        # it these tokens are appended to the request's output and streamed
        # to the client as if they were valid continuations of the prompt.
        num_reserved = request.num_output_placeholders
        logger.warning_once(
            "Model runner returned more tokens than there were reserved output "
            "placeholders; dropping the extra token(s). A token sampled while "
            "the request is still prefilling is not a valid continuation of the "
            "prompt, so it must not be appended to the response or streamed to "
            "the client. Run with debug logging to see which requests are "
            "affected.",
        )
        logger.debug(
            "Request %s: model runner returned %d token(s) but only %d output "
            "placeholder(s) were reserved; dropping %d token(s).",
            request.request_id,
            len(new_token_ids),
            num_reserved,
            len(new_token_ids) - num_reserved,
        )
        new_token_ids = new_token_ids[:num_reserved]

    new_token_ids, stopped = super()._update_request_with_output(
        request, new_token_ids
    )
    ...
```

The truncation happens before `super()` because the parent appends the tokens to the request as a side effect, and it must only append tokens that were reserved for.

**On log volume.** The warning is `warning_once`, not `warning`: in the #57562 scenario the condition repeats every prefill step, and a per-occurrence warning produced 44 lines in a single 12-request load. Per-request detail -- request id, delivered, reserved, and how many were dropped -- is emitted at `debug` level instead, so it stays available on demand without flooding production logs.

**Trade-off:** on the realtime path described in #30142 the excess tokens are genuinely sampled and dropping them truncates the response. This PR still drops them -- the alternative is killing the engine and every other in-flight request with it. The warning makes the loss attributable rather than silent. If maintainers prefer a different degradation policy for that path, the guard is the single place to change it.

## Testing

Two CPU unit tests in `tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py`:

- `test_prefill_chunk_token_delivery_does_not_underflow` -- schedules a prompt that cannot fit in one chunk, so the request is a prefill chunk with zero placeholders, then delivers a token for it. Before this PR this fails with `AssertionError` at `async_scheduler.py:63`; after, the placeholder count stays at 0 and the token is not appended.
- `test_async_placeholder_consumed_by_decode_delivery` -- pins the healthy path, so the guard cannot start dropping legitimate decode tokens.

```
$ python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q
```

**Negative control, re-run against current `main`.** The PR was opened against an older base, so this was re-measured on `main @ 8ee4069033` by swapping only `async_scheduler.py` between the two arms:

```
ARM A  main (unpatched)   FAILED test_prefill_chunk_token_delivery_does_not_underflow
                          vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py:71: AssertionError
                          > assert request.num_output_placeholders >= 0
                          1 failed, 1 passed, 21 deselected
ARM B  with this PR       2 passed, 21 deselected
```

The synthetic trigger still reproduces on current `main`, months of scheduler drift later, and the guard still converts it into a drop. The healthy-path test passes in both arms, which is the control that the guard does not fire on legitimate decode deliveries. (The assert is at line 71 on current `main`, not 63 as quoted in [Problem](#problem), which is a verbatim quote of the 0.29.0 stack trace from the issue.)

**On the test's mock.** `_make_model_runner_output` returns a token for every scheduled request, including prefill chunks -- it does not mirror the runner's discard mask. That is deliberate: the mock models the *observed worker behaviour* in #57562, where the delivered-token set and the scheduler's reservation disagreed. A mock that reimplemented the runner's predicate would assume away the exact disagreement this test exists to catch. What the test pins is the scheduler's response to over-delivery, which is the part this PR changes.

**Regression check.** `pytest -m cpu_test tests/v1/core/` (excluding `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache`, which has an unrelated `anthropic` import error in this environment) run against the patched tree and against the identical tree reverted to HEAD, then the two failure sets diffed: identical (51 pre-existing environment failures in both, from a `torchvision` incompatibility in this container; 595 passed patched vs 592 reverted, the +3 being this PR's tests plus the repro file). No test changed state.

Lint: `ruff 0.15.12`, the version pinned in `requirements/docs.txt`, clean on both files.

## Trigger 2: the resumable-request path (#50692)

@yeighta asked whether the guard is still wanted for the resumable-request path. I checked it, and the honest answer is that **I could not reproduce that divergence on current `main`, so I am not claiming the clamp covers it.**

The mechanism #50692 addressed, as reported by @twu3202: for streaming updates (#35755) a segment can end on a stop token while the next decode is still in flight, and the next chunk is applied before that step is delivered. The stale placeholder made `is_prefill_chunk` true for the full-sequence chunk; `_update_after_schedule` then skipped the reservation and the two deliveries drove the counter to -1.

@twu3202 posted a CPU reproducer that he measured as failing on `main` at `144e79c` and passing with #50692. I appended that reproducer verbatim (with only the `max_num_seqs=1` fix he noted) to `tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py` and ran it on `main @ 8ee4069033` twice -- once unpatched, once with this PR's clamp applied:

```
ARM A  main (unpatched)  tests/.../test_async_scheduler.py:851: AssertionError
                         assert 0 == 1
                         where 0 = <Request>.num_output_placeholders
ARM B  with this PR      identical failure, identical counters
```

Both arms fail at the reproducer's *first* assertion and neither ever reaches the underflow. Instrumenting the same sequence shows the counter balancing to zero with no underflow (`underflow_error: null`), with the same values in both arms:

```json
{"placeholders_after_prefill_delivery": 0,
 "placeholders_after_new_chunk_sched": 1,
 "placeholders_after_inflight_delivery": 1,
 "placeholders_after_final_delivery": 0,
 "is_prefill_chunk_at_new_chunk": false,
 "underflow_error": null}
```

The reason is that the path has since been fixed at its source. **#58259 "[Bugfix] Fix resumable request + async scheduling handoff race"** (merged 2026-09-28, after @twu3202's base) zeroes the placeholders on the resumable handoff, which removes exactly the stale placeholder he identified as the cause:

```python
# Drop the finished turn's in-flight work and resume from the
# materialized frontier.
safe_frontier = request.num_computed_tokens - request.num_output_placeholders
assert safe_frontier >= 0
request.num_computed_tokens = safe_frontier
request.spec_token_ids = []
request.drop_stale_output = True
request.num_stale_output_tokens = request.num_in_flight_tokens
request.num_output_placeholders = 0
```

With the placeholder zeroed, `is_prefill_chunk` is no longer wrongly true for the continuation chunk, the reservation is no longer skipped, and the arithmetic balances. The two arms are byte-identical because neither one fires the guard -- this is a negative result for the clamp on that path, not evidence for it.

**So:** the resumable path does not justify the guard today. If it later regresses, the clamp's condition (`len(new_token_ids) > num_output_placeholders`) is the same arithmetic that underflowed there, so it would convert that assert into a dropped token rather than a dead engine -- but that is reasoning from @twu3202's trace, not something I measured, and I am not putting it forward as verification.

## Model evaluation

**No model evaluation was run by me.** AGENTS.md asks for eval results on changes that affect serving output, and this change does affect serving output -- in the over-delivery case it drops tokens instead of crashing. I am disclosing the gap rather than omitting it, because the evidence here is CPU-only:

- The verification environment is CPU (`torch` CPU build, WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04), with no GPU available.
- The failure being guarded is a scheduler bookkeeping bug, not a model-output discrepancy, so the CPU unit tests exercise the changed code path directly.
- What a GPU eval would add is confirmation that the guard does not fire on healthy decode paths under concurrent load. `test_async_placeholder_consumed_by_decode_delivery` covers that at the unit level, and real-model runs are recorded in [Hardware validation](#hardware-validation) -- run by @yeighta on hardware this environment does not have. They are their measurements, not mine, and they are attributed as such.

If a reviewer wants the eval before considering this, say so and I will flag that it needs a GPU machine -- this PR should not be treated as having been evaluated end-to-end.

## Hardware validation

All runs and measurements in this section are by @yeighta ([reporter of #57562](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57562)), on the machine that reproduces the issue. They are split into the original reproduction and the post-fix re-measurement, because the two support different claims.

### Historical: what the clamp does when the divergence happens (vLLM 0.29.0, before #57404 / #57415)

Azure NCC H100 NVL 94GB, SEV-SNP with the GPU in Confidential Computing mode, vLLM 0.29.0 (cu129), `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8`, `--max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 64 --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill`, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, with commit `8953680` of this branch applied to the installed package, 12 requests (6 concurrent x 2 rounds). Baseline on the same machine before patching: EngineCore died about 2 s in at `async_scheduler.py:63`, `/health` 503, 6 requests into round 1.

| question | answer from the run |
| --- | --- |
| does the load complete instead of killing EngineCore? | yes -- `round 1: ok=6/6 alive=True`, `round 2: ok=6/6 alive=True`, `engine_alive fatal=0/12 rejected_4xx=0`, `health=200 NRestarts=0` |
| does the guard fire on healthy decode steps? | no -- 42 drops across 5 of the 12 requests, every one of them with `num_output_placeholders == 0` and none with a non-zero reservation |
| how many times does `warning_once` fire? | exactly 1, over a run that dropped 42 tokens |

This is the record of the guard's behaviour *when the divergence happens*, and it remains the evidence for the middle question -- that the guard fires only on zero-reservation over-deliveries and never on healthy decode steps. It is retained as a historical measurement of the pre-fix stack.

Two findings from the same run that are **not** about this patch, recorded because they change what the surrounding issue means:

- On that machine the responses are garbage (`!` repeated, token id 0) on the V2 model runner under CC. It is present with and without the guard and disappears on V1, so it is #57224 rather than a consequence of dropping tokens. It also answers, with a measurement, the question this description previously left as an argument: the tokens the guard drops were already unusable.
- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` eliminates the underflow entirely on that machine -- 0 events under the identical load that produces 42 with V2. That is the evidence for the "which side" paragraph in [Mechanism](#mechanism): the scheduler is not what differs between those runs.

### Post-fix: the current state (vLLM 0.30.0, with #57404 or #57415)

Same machine, same 12-request chunked-prefill repro, **no clamp applied**, `vllm==0.30.0`, torch 2.13.0+cu130. Each PR is its current head (`946356a8`, `51562a76`) with only its `vllm/` files applied to the 0.30.0 wheel. Full table and setup: [#57224 comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57224#issuecomment-5910454602).

| config | correctness (8 greedy prompts vs V1) | c=1 tok/s | c=12 tok/s | #57562 repro |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| V1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) | reference | 149.6 | 1193.9 | 12/12, engine alive |
| V2, unpatched | 0/8, random multilingual tokens | 39.6, bimodal | 310.4 | EngineCore dies in round 1, `assert request.num_output_placeholders >= 0` |
| V2 + #57404 | **8/8 identical to V1** | 147.7 | 1328.0 | 12/12, engine alive |
| V2 + #57415 | **8/8 identical to V1** | 154.3 | 1367.8 | 12/12, engine alive |

**The assert was still in place in both patched runs**, so the engine surviving 12/12 means no underflow occurred at all -- the clamp is not what kept those runs alive, and would not even have been reached. That is the measurement behind the rewrite in [Status of the triggers](#status-of-the-triggers-that-motivated-this-pr-updated-2026-09-30): on this trigger the clamp is a backstop, and the source-level fix is what makes the path correct.

## Relationship to other open work

**Duplicate-work check (AGENTS.md Section1).** I searched open PRs before opening this one:

```
$ gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "num_output_placeholders"
# 14 results
```

None of the 14 changes the delivery side of `_update_request_with_output`. The PRs below each fix a *different trigger* of the same invariant, at that trigger's own call site; none of them makes the invariant non-fatal for a divergence that has not been found yet. That last part is what this PR does, and it is the only part still doing work now that #57404 / #57415 and #58259 have landed. The remaining search hits match the identifier incidentally (unrelated features, docs, KV-connector work).

- **#50692** (the PR, not the issue) is **closed, not merged** -- superseded on its own path by #58259. It was the reservation-side PR that would have made `_update_after_schedule` reserve for streaming updates (#35755). @twu3202 ran it against `main` @ `144e79c` with Qwen3-ASR-0.6B in realtime mode on an RTX 6000 Ada and confirmed that `main` died on `async_scheduler.py:63` after ~16 s while the patched tree completed a 60 s session. Its own regression test did not guard the change -- @twu3202 reported that it passes on unpatched `main`, and supplied a corrected reproducer -- and that corrected reproducer no longer reaches the underflow on current `main` either, for the reason given in [Trigger 2](#trigger-2-the-resumable-request-path-50692).
- #45146 / #45430 reset placeholders on the KV-load-failure recompute path; #43683 clears them in the streaming session rebuild path. Those are other triggers of the same invariant, handled at their own call sites.

## Compatibility

No API or config change. Behaviour differs only in the case that previously crashed EngineCore.

## Notes

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). The reproduction, the tests, and the verification runs above were executed as described; the root-cause analysis was reviewed by hand against the sources at the commit listed.

Test environment: commit `53f897c3` for the original run, `8ee4069033` for the re-run in [Testing](#testing), CPU (`torch` CPU build), `pytest -m cpu_test`, WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 / Python 3.12.

items.title: [Performance] Incremental strip of covered mm data to avoid O(n^2) scheduler work in realtime sessions
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58324.

`NewRequestData.from_request()` called `strip_covered_mm_data()` over the request's entire `mm_features` list on every scheduling step. For realtime (streaming-input) sessions — which append one multimodal feature per 80 ms audio chunk and are re-scheduled on every chunk — this walks and rebuilds (via `dataclasses.replace`) every accumulated feature each step. As profiled in #58324, scheduler time grows linearly with session age (~3 ms/min of audio; `strip_covered_mm_data` took 55.9 % of EngineCore wall time at ~9 min on a Voxtral-Mini realtime session), i.e. quadratic total work, eventually missing the 80 ms real-time budget.

The covered set only grows: `request.num_computed_tokens` is monotonic and features are appended in increasing `mm_position.offset` order (the same ordering `get_mm_features_in_window` already relies on). The stripped form of a feature is therefore stable once computed.

This PR adds `strip_covered_mm_data_incremental()`, which keeps the already-stripped prefix on the `Request` (`_mm_stripped_mm_features` / `_mm_strip_cursor`) and only inspects features appended since the previous scheduling step. Per-step cost drops from O(total features) to O(new features). The pure `strip_covered_mm_data()` is left unchanged for direct callers and its existing tests.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_output.py -v
ruff check vllm/multimodal/utils.py vllm/v1/request.py \
    vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py tests/v1/core/test_output.py
ruff format --check vllm/multimodal/utils.py vllm/v1/request.py \
    vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py tests/v1/core/test_output.py
```

New tests in `tests/v1/core/test_output.py`:

- `test_strip_covered_incremental_matches_pure`: the incremental result equals the pure `strip_covered_mm_data` at every prefix size 0..400, including `data=None` and boundary spans.
- `test_strip_covered_incremental_advances_only`: the cursor advances only over newly covered features, and previously stripped objects are reused instead of rebuilt.
- `test_strip_covered_incremental_appended_features`: simulates a realtime session where features are appended between scheduling steps.

## Test Result

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on the four changed files.

CPU logic check mirroring the tests (the strip path is pure Python):

- 750 accumulated audio features (~12 min Voxtral session), subsequent steps: **~5 us/step** with this change vs the reported **~3000 us/step** (2.99 ms/min slope) on main.
- Streaming growth (one new feature per step): flat ~5 us/step instead of quadratic.
- Behavior is identical to the old implementation: covered features get `data=None` (or only keep-on-CPU fields with `uses_mrope=True`), `data=None` and `address` items pass through unchanged, and the scheduler-side request features are never mutated.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Report the unreported ancestor of a partial prefix-cache entry
items.body:
## Purpose

Make the KV-cache event stream reconstructable when a partial prefix-cache entry
references a parent hash that no event reported.

Fixes #58119

## Problem

An external consumer of the KV-cache event stream cannot attach a partial entry
to its prefix chain, because the entry's parent may never have been emitted.

With `hash_block_size=128`, `block_size=1536` and an 1800-token request, the
emitted events are:

```json
{"block_hashes": ["H1536"], "parent_block_hash": null,    "token_ids": [0, 1536),    "block_size": 1536}
{"block_hashes": ["H1792"], "parent_block_hash": "H1664",  "token_ids": [1664, 1792), "block_size": 128}
```

`H1664` is reported by no event, and the second event carries nothing else that
lets a consumer place it in the chain.

## Root Cause

A granularity mismatch between the two event producers in
`vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py`:

- `cache_full_blocks()` reports `block_hashes` from
  `resolve_block_hashes(..., block_size)` — one hash per **cache block**
  (1536 tokens), so only `H1536` is reported.
- `cache_partial_block()` describes a **hash-block-sized** chunk: its parent comes
  from `_get_partial_block_parent_hash_and_start()`, so `H1792` names the
  fine-grained boundary `H1664`, which nothing reports.

The partial event's fine-grained shape must stay as it is: it is pinned by
`test_cache_partial_block_kv_cache_events`.

## Solution

Emit the boundary (or boundaries) between the last reported block-aligned
ancestor and the partial entry, so every parent reference in the stream resolves
to a reported hash. For the example above the stream becomes:

```json
{"block_hashes": ["H1536"], "parent_block_hash": null,    "token_ids": [0, 1536)}
{"block_hashes": ["H1664"], "parent_block_hash": "H1536", "token_ids": [1536, 1664)}
{"block_hashes": ["H1792"], "parent_block_hash": "H1664", "token_ids": [1664, 1792)}
```

Two deliberate restrictions:

- **No event schema change.** See "Rejected alternative" below.
- **Only first-time partial registrations are filled.** A promotion has already
  described its own boundaries and reports their removal, so re-reporting them
  would resurrect hashes that were just removed; that case would also change the
  event sequence pinned by
  `test_partial_block_replacement_emits_remove_then_store_events`. Nothing is
  emitted when the entry lies in the first cache block, because there is no
  reported ancestor to attach to.

### Prior art in tree

`OffloadingEventsTracker._build_partial_tail_metadata()`
(`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/events.py`) already
solves the same problem for a partial tail, and does it by making the ancestry
explicit inside the event:

```python
chunk_start = ((boundary_tokens - 1) // tokens_per_chunk) * tokens_per_chunk
first_hash_idx = chunk_start // tokens_per_hash
last_hash_idx = boundary_tokens // tokens_per_hash
block_hashes = req.block_hashes[first_hash_idx:last_hash_idx]   # every hash in the span
parent_block_hash = req.block_hashes[first_hash_idx - 1] if first_hash_idx > 0 else None
assert first_hash_idx == 0 or parent_block_hash is not None
```

For the configuration in this report that produces
`block_hashes=[H1664, H1792]` with `parent_block_hash=H1536`, so the chain closes
with no extra events. The core's partial entry cannot adopt that shape without
changing `test_cache_partial_block_kv_cache_events`, which pins a **single-element**
`block_hashes` and a fine-grained parent.

A second implementation already does what this patch does.
`SimpleCPUOffloadManager` (`vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py`, ~line 903)
emits **one event per fine-grained boundary** inside a stored group block, each
covering exactly one hash block and parented to the immediately preceding
boundary:

```python
first_hash_idx = token_start // self.hash_block_size
last_hash_idx = token_end // self.hash_block_size
for hash_idx in range(first_hash_idx, last_hash_idx):
    ...
    meta_by_hash[block_hash] = BlockStoreMeta(
        token_ids=list(request.all_token_ids[hash_start:hash_end]),
        parent_block_hash=(
            None if hash_idx == 0
            else maybe_convert_block_hash(request.block_hashes[hash_idx - 1])
        ),
        block_size=self.hash_block_size,
    )
```

That is the same shape as the events this patch adds for the core's partial entry,
so the core's stream ends up consistent with what the offload path already
produces for the same tokens.

(For completeness: `mooncake/store/worker.py` derives its parent from the request's
hash chain and its own comment notes that "Store filtering can separate adjacent
request blocks", so the same class of gap is already recognised in the connector
layer; it is not touched here.)

### Rejected alternative

Adding optional `skipped_parent_block_hash` / `skipped_token_ids` fields to
`BlockStored` and pointing `parent_block_hash` at the last reported ancestor.
This was implemented and abandoned, because it silently changes the wire format
for **every** event: `BlockStored` had 14 declared fields and a tagged struct
encodes as a map, so msgspec sized the header from the declared field count. At
15 entries (14 fields + tag) it fits msgpack's one-byte `fixmap` header; adding
two fields pushes it to 17 and every payload switches to a three-byte `map16`
header:

```
old: \x8c          (fixmap, 12 entries) -> 221 bytes
new: \xde\x00\x0c  (map16,  12 entries) -> 223 bytes
```

`tests/distributed/test_kv_cache_events.py` exists precisely to prevent that
(`_LegacyBlockStored`, `_PreSessionBlockStored`), and it failed for the two
pre-existing wire-compatibility tests under that approach — which is how this
was caught. The schema-free version keeps those tests green.

## Known remaining case (deliberately not addressed here)

The same bug class also exists on the **promotion** path. When an existing partial
entry moves to a later boundary, the pool emits `BlockRemoved` for the old
boundary and a `BlockStored` whose `parent_block_hash` is *that removed hash*, so
the parent is again unresolved in the stream:

```
Removed hashes=['0xb92e76c1']
Stored  hashes=['0xdeab6e27'] parent=0xb92e76c1
parent reported in this batch? False
```

It is not fixed here on purpose. The current behaviour is pinned by
`test_partial_block_replacement_emits_remove_then_store_events`, which asserts
both `len(events) == 2` and that the stored event's parent is the removed
boundary. Changing it requires deciding whether a promotion should re-report the
boundary it just removed or instead point its parent at the last surviving
ancestor. **Tracked separately as #58394** (with a runnable repro and its actual
output), so it does not widen this PR's scope — happy to fold it in here if you
would prefer that.

## Compatibility

No schema change, so payloads are byte-for-byte identical to `main` — verified by
the existing wire-compatibility tests. The only observable difference is the
additional `BlockStored` events for boundaries that were previously missing from
the stream, which is the point of the fix.
